## Getting Food Help in California You’ve lost your job and need help buying food. Below is a quick guide to the main programs that can help you right now, how to apply, what you’ll need, and where to look for extra support. --- ### 1. CalFresh (California’s SNAP program) | What it is | Who can get it | How you get it | How long it takes | |------------|----------------|----------------|-------------------| | A monthly benefit loaded onto an **Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) card** that you use like a debit card to buy groceries. | • Adults (including you) who live in California and meet income‑and‑resource limits.
• Most legal residents, U.S. citizens, and many qualified non‑citizens.
• Household income must be **at or below 200 % of the Federal Poverty Level** (the exact dollar amount changes each year). | 1. **Apply online** at or .
2. Call your **County Social Services Agency** if you need help with the application or an interpreter.
3. After the agency reviews your paperwork, they will mail or give you an EBT card. | • **Expedited (same‑day) service**: if you qualify for emergency need, you can receive benefits within **3 days**.
• Regular processing: eligibility is usually decided within **30 days** of filing. | #### Steps to apply 1. **Gather basic info** – name, address, phone, Social Security number (or ITIN if you’re a qualified non‑citizen). 2. **Collect documents** – recent pay stubs, bank statements, unemployment benefits (EDD), rent/mortgage bill, and any other income (child support, SSI, etc.). 3. **Create an online account** on the CalFresh portal and fill out the short questionnaire. 4. **Submit proof** of income and residence. You can upload scans or bring paper copies to your county office. 5. **Interview** – a county staff member may call or meet with you (often by phone) to confirm details. 6. **Receive your EBT card** – sign it, set a PIN, and start buying food. #### What you can buy with CalFresh - Almost all groceries: fruits, vegetables, meat, dairy, bread, cereal. - Seeds & plants to grow your own food. - Some nutrition items for infants and toddlers (WIC items are separate). You **cannot** buy alcohol, tobacco, pet food, prepared hot meals, or non‑food items like soap or toothpaste. #### Who to call for help - **CalFresh Benefits Helpline:** 1‑877‑847‑3663 (available 24 hours). - Your local **County Social Services Agency** – find the phone number on the county’s website or at . --- ### 2. Local Food Banks & Emergency Food Programs If you need food right now while you wait for CalFresh, go to a food bank or pantry. | County (example) | Food Bank / Agency | Phone | Address | |------------------|-------------------|-------|----------| | Alameda | Alameda County Social Services – General Assistance | 510‑555‑1234 | 1 New Street, Oakland | | Monterey | Monterey County Food Bank | 831‑758‑1523 | 353 W Rossi St, Salinas | | Ventura | Ventura County Food Share | 805‑983‑7100 | 4156 N Southbank Rd, Oxnard | | Yolo | Yolo County Food Bank | 530‑668‑0690 | 233 Harter Ave, Woodland | | *All other counties* | Search “County Food Bank California” or dial **2‑1‑1** for the nearest location. | **How to use the food bank:** - Call ahead to confirm hours and any ID requirements. - Many banks let you walk in with no ID; some ask just for proof of residence (a lease or mail). - You can receive a bag of non‑perishable items, fresh produce, or a “food pantry card” that works like an EBT card at participating stores. --- ### 3. Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) If you are pregnant, have a baby, or have a child under 5, you may qualify for **WIC**, which gives vouchers for healthy foods (milk, cheese, fruits, vegetables, whole grains, infant formula). - **Apply** at your local County Health Department or call the WIC hotline at **1‑800‑942‑4623**. - You’ll need proof of pregnancy or a child’s birth certificate, plus proof of income (same limits as CalFresh). --- ### 4. Other Programs That May Help | Program | What it offers | Who may qualify | |---------|----------------|-----------------| | **CalWORKs** (California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids) | Cash aid plus food assistance for families with children; also provides job‑training services. | Low‑income families with children under 18 (or 19 if still in high school). | | **Emergency Assistance (EA)** | One‑time cash or vouchers for food, rent, utilities when you face an urgent shortfall. | Anyone in crisis; amounts and eligibility vary by county. | | **Medi‑Cal** (California’s Medicaid) | Free or low‑cost health coverage; includes nutrition counseling and sometimes food‑related programs. | Same income limits as CalFresh; many applicants qualify for both. | | **Community Action Agency (CAA) Programs** | Local job training, transportation vouchers, and sometimes “food assistance cards.” | Residents of the agency’s service area; often open to all low‑income adults. | | **211** | Free 24‑hour helpline that connects you to food, housing, and other emergency services in your neighborhood. | Anyone who dials **2‑1‑1**. | --- ### 5. Timeline Overview | Step | Approximate time | |------|----------------| | Online CalFresh application | Immediate (minutes) | | Submit documents | Same day or within a few days | | County review & interview | Up to **30 days** (often quicker) | | Receive EBT card (regular) | **2‑3 weeks** after approval | | Expedited emergency benefits | **3 days** (if you qualify for “Immediate Need”) | | Food bank visit | Same day you go, no wait | --- ## What to Do Next 1. **Start the CalFresh application now** – it’s free and can be done on your phone or computer. 2. **Call 2‑1‑1** or look up your county’s food‑bank list if you need food today. 3. **Check if you or a child qualify for WIC** – that can add extra nutrition items right away. 4. **Keep copies of all documents** (pay stubs, unemployment awards, rent statements) in a folder so you can upload or bring them quickly. 5. **Ask the county staff** about **CalWORKs** or **Emergency Assistance** if you have children or other urgent bills. --- ### Quick Links - Apply for CalFresh: - CalFresh Help Helpline: 1‑877‑847‑3663 - Find your county food bank: - WIC hotline: 1‑800‑942‑4623 - 2‑1‑1 (general referrals): dial **2‑1‑1** --- You’re not alone—many Californians rely on these programs when work is lost. Take the first step today, and you’ll have food on the table soon. If you need help filling out the application, a county worker or a local nonprofit can walk you through it for free. Stay hopeful—you have resources available. 🌱

question: Can I recieve multiple types of assistance at the same time?
answer:
## You Can Get More Than One Benefit at a Time  

Many people who have lost a job qualify for **two or more programs** at once.  The state tries to make sure you get the help you need without “double‑paying” for the same thing.  Below is a simple guide to the most common overlaps, what you’ll need, and how to apply.

---

### 1. What Programs Often Stack Together  

| Program | What it Covers | Can it be combined with…? |
|---------|----------------|----------------------------|
| **Unemployment Insurance (UI)** | Weekly cash benefits while you look for work | ✅ **CalFresh** (food), ✅ **Medi‑Cal**, ✅ **Lifeline**, ✅ **CalWORKs** (if you’re a parent) |
| **CalFresh (SNAP)** | Monthly food assistance | ✅ UI, ✅ **Medi‑Cal**, ✅ **Lifeline**, ✅ **General Assistance** (cash) |
| **Medi‑Cal** (California Medicaid) | Health care, doctor visits, prescriptions | ✅ UI, ✅ CalFresh, ✅ **Lifeline**, ✅ **General Assistance** |
| **CalWORKs** (TANF) | Cash aid, child care, work‑training for families with kids | ✅ UI (if you have kids), ✅ **CalFresh**, ✅ **Medi‑Cal**, ✅ **Lifeline** |
| **General Assistance (GA)** | Cash help for adults who are not eligible for CalWORKs | ✅ UI, ✅ CalFresh, ✅ **Medi‑Cal**, ✅ **Lifeline** (but GA is a loan you must repay) |
| **Lifeline (phone/Internet discount)** | Discount on phone or broadband | ✅ Any of the above programs (you just need a benefit letter) |
| **SSI or SSDI** (federal disability) | Cash for disabled adults or seniors | ✅ **Medi‑Cal**, ✅ **CalFresh**, ✅ **Lifeline** (but SSI earnings limits may affect UI eligibility) |
| **Veterans’ Benefits** | Cash, health, housing help | ✅ Most other state programs (check VA and county rules) |

**Key point:** Most cash‑benefit programs (UI, CalWORKs, GA) can be paid **at the same time**, but each program looks at your total household income and resources.  If one program says “you must be unemployable,” you may still get UI if you’re actively looking for work.

---

### 2. Basic Eligibility Rules to Keep in Mind  

| Program | Typical Eligibility |
|---------|----------------------|
| **UI** | Lost job through no fault of your own, earned enough wages in the past 12‑18 months, able and available to work. |
| **CalFresh** | Household income ≤ 165 % of the federal poverty level; includes UI, GA, or SSI income. |
| **Medi‑Cal** | Income ≤ 138 % of FPL for adults; higher limits for children, pregnant people, or seniors. |
| **CalWORKs** | Must have a minor child (or be pregnant) and meet income/resource limits; usually 60 months total benefit. |
| **General Assistance** | Adults without minor children, low‑income, not eligible for CalWORKs.  County‑specific limits (often 3 months in any 12‑month period unless exempt). |
| **Lifeline** | Must be enrolled in *any* qualifying public assistance program (Medi‑Cal, CalFresh, SSI, etc.) **or** have income ≤ $25,000 (individual) / $38,000 (household). |
| **SSI/SSDI** | Federal disability criteria; income limits are very low for SSI. |
| **Veterans’ Benefits** | Service‑connected disability, pension, or survivor status. |

*Eligibility can vary a little from county to county, especially for General Assistance and some local housing programs.*

---

### 3. How to Apply for Multiple Benefits  

1. **Gather your documents** (see the list below).  
2. **Start with the program that is easiest to apply for** – often UI (online at EDD) or CalFresh (online at GetCalFresh).  
3. **Tell the caseworker you are applying for other benefits.**  Most county agencies can submit your information to other programs for you.  
4. **Complete each application** (online, phone, or in‑person).  Keep a copy of every confirmation number.  
5. **Follow up** within 2‑4 weeks to check status.  If you get approved for one benefit, the agency may automatically forward your eligibility to related programs (e.g., UI → CalFresh).  

#### Where to Apply  

- **Unemployment Insurance:** [EDD UI portal](https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/) – create an account, fill out the claim, and register in CalJOBS.  
- **CalFresh:** [GetCalFresh.org](https://www.getcalfresh.org/) – single‑page online application.  
- **Medi‑Cal:** Apply online at [Covered California](https://www.coveredca.com/) or at your county social services office.  
- **CalWORKs:** County Social Services Agency (SSA) – you can apply online, by phone, or in person.  
- **General Assistance:** County SSA (same application as CalWORKs; choose “General Assistance” on the form).  
- **Lifeline:** Apply through your phone or internet provider; you’ll need a benefit letter from any qualifying program.  

---

### 4. Documents You’ll Usually Need  

| Category | Examples |
|----------|----------|
| **Identification** | Driver’s license, state ID, or passport; proof of birth (if needed). |
| **Proof of Residency** | Utility bill, rental agreement, or mail with your name and address (dated within last 60 days). |
| **Income Proof** | Recent pay stubs, UI claim confirmation, unemployment benefit letter, SSI award letter, bank statements (last 30 days). |
| **Benefit Letters** | Any letter showing enrollment in Medi‑Cal, CalFresh, SSI, VA benefits, etc. (required for Lifeline). |
| **Social Security Number** | Needed for all state/federal programs. |
| **Employment History** | Last 12‑18 months of employer names and addresses (for UI). |
| **Disability Documents** (if applicable) | Doctor’s letter, SSDI/SSI award notice. |
| **Student Status** (if you’re a student) | Enrollment verification, transcript, or financial aid award letter (needed for CalFresh student eligibility). |

---

### 5. Timelines – What to Expect  

| Program | Typical Processing Time |
|---------|--------------------------|
| **UI** | 2‑3 weeks for first payment after you file and certify. |
| **CalFresh** | 30 days (or less with expedited “Emergency” assistance). |
| **Medi‑Cal** | 30‑45 days (faster if you apply through Covered California). |
| **CalWORKs** | 30‑45 days after you submit a complete application. |
| **General Assistance** | 30 days; cash may be issued as a lump sum or monthly after approval. |
| **Lifeline** | Usually within 2 weeks after you send a benefit letter. |

*If you need money fast, ask the county caseworker about “Emergency” CalFresh or a **One‑Time Assistance** grant; many counties have short‑term cash programs.*

---

### 6. Helpful Tips  

- **Apply even if you think you might not qualify.**  The agency will tell you, and you won’t lose anything by trying.  
- **Keep a “benefits folder”** (paper or digital) with copies of every application and any letters you receive.  
- **Tell each program about the others** you’re receiving.  It avoids over‑payments that later need to be repaid.  
- **Ask about “mandatory work activities.”**  CalWORKs, GA, and some UI extensions require you to attend job‑search classes or training.  
- **Look for local “one‑stop” centers** (often at the county SSA office) where you can fill out several forms in one visit.  
- **If you’re a veteran or on tribal lands,** check the VA or tribal assistance offices— they often have extra cash or housing help that can be layered on top of state benefits.  

---

## Quick “Can I Get Multiple Benefits?” Checklist  

| ✅ | Question |
|---|----------|
| ✅ | Do I have UI benefits? (Apply first at EDD.) |
| ✅ | Does my household income fall below the CalFresh limit? (Apply at GetCalFresh.) |
| ✅ | Am I eligible for Medi‑Cal? (Apply online or at the county office.) |
| ✅ | Do I have dependent children or am I pregnant? (You may qualify for CalWORKs.) |
| ✅ | Am I a non‑citizen, senior, or disabled adult not covered by CalWORKs? (Check General Assistance or CAPI.) |
| ✅ | Do I already have a qualifying benefit (Medi‑Cal, CalFresh, SSI, VA, etc.)? (You can use that to get Lifeline.) |
| ✅ | Have I gathered all required documents? |
| ✅ | Have I told each program about the others I’m receiving? |

If you answer “yes” to several of these, you can likely receive **multiple benefits at the same time**.

---

### Need More Help?  

- **County Social Services Agency** – call the local office (phone numbers are on each county’s website).  
- **California Employment Development Department (EDD)** – for UI and job‑search resources.  
- **Legal Aid or “Self‑Help” centers** – free assistance with applications and appeals.  
- **Veterans Services Office** – if you have military benefits.  

You’re not alone—many Californians navigate several programs after a job loss.  Start with the application that’s easiest for you, keep your paperwork organized, and let the county caseworkers know you’re interested in all the help you may qualify for.  Good luck, and take one step at a time!

question: Do I qualify for WIC in California?
answer:
## Quick Check: Could You Qualify for California WIC?  

| You must meet all of these conditions | What it means for you |
|---|---|
| **Pregnant, breast‑feeding, chest‑feeding, or had a baby (or pregnancy loss) in the last 6 months** | You are in one of the “maternal” categories the program serves. |
| **Or** you **care for a child under 5 years old** | If you have a preschool‑age child you can apply for the child’s benefits. |
| **Low‑to‑medium household income** *or* you already receive **Medi‑Cal, CalWORKs (TANF), or CalFresh (SNAP)** | The program is income‑based, but having one of the listed benefits automatically meets the income test. |
| **Live in California** | You must have a California address (you can use a rental agreement, utility bill, etc.). |
| **U.S. citizen or eligible non‑citizen** | Most lawful residents qualify; the state does not share your immigration status with federal agencies. |

If you check **yes** for the first two rows and meet the income/benefits rule, you are likely eligible. The only way to be sure is to have a local WIC office confirm it.

---

## How to Apply  

1. **Find a WIC office**  
   * Call the toll‑free line **1‑800‑852‑5770** (Mon‑Fri 8 a.m.–5 p.m.) *or* use the [WIC office locator](https://myfamily.wic.ca.gov/Home/HowCanIGetWIC) to search by city or ZIP code.  

2. **Make an appointment**  
   * Most counties require a scheduled visit (phone or online).  

3. **Gather documents for your first appointment**  

   | Document | Why you need it |
   |---|---|
   | Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID, passport) for you and any children under 5 | Verifies identity and age |
   | Proof of California address (utility bill, lease, paycheck with address) | Shows residency |
   | Proof of income (pay stubs, recent tax return, employer letter) *or* a Medi‑Cal, CalWORKs, or CalFresh card | Shows you meet the income test |
   | Proof of pregnancy (prenatal visit note, ultrasound report) *if applicable* | Confirms maternal eligibility |
   | Medical forms from your health‑care provider (for infants) | Needed for newborn/infant enrollment |
   | Birth certificate for any child you’re enrolling | Confirms age (under 5) |

4. **Attend the appointment**  
   * A WIC counselor will review your paperwork, ask a few health‑related questions, and complete a nutrition assessment for each family member you’re enrolling.  

5. **Receive your WIC Card**  
   * Once approved, your food benefits are loaded onto a **single California WIC Card** that you can use right away at participating stores.  

6. **Start using benefits**  
   * Use the free **California WIC App** (iOS or Android) to check your food balance, find participating retailers, and see which brands are covered.  

---

## Typical Timeline  

| Step | Approximate time |
|---|---|
| Call/online appointment request | Same day or within a few days |
| First appointment (paperwork review) | Usually within 1‑2 weeks, but can vary by county |
| Card issuance & first benefit loading | Same day or within a few days after approval |
| Ongoing benefits | Monthly reloads (often on the same calendar day each month) |

*Note:* **County processes can differ**—some offices may have longer wait times or require additional forms. Always ask the local office what their specific timeline looks like.

---

## Other Programs That May Help You  

| Program | Who it serves | What it provides |
|---|---|---|
| **CalFresh (SNAP)** | Low‑income households of any size | Monthly food benefits that can be used at most grocery stores |
| **Medi‑Cal** | Residents who meet income limits | Free or low‑cost health coverage (doctor visits, prescriptions, etc.) |
| **CalWORKs (TANF)** | Families with children who need cash assistance & services | Money for basic needs, job training, child‑care assistance |
| **Unemployment Insurance (UI)** | Workers who lost a job through no fault of their own | Weekly cash benefits while you look for new work |
| **Housing Assistance (Section 8, HUD, local programs)** | Low‑income households | Rental subsidies or emergency housing help |

Even if you already receive one of these benefits, you can still apply for WIC. The programs are designed to work together.

---

## Helpful Resources  

* **WIC Office Locator & Phone:** 1‑800‑852‑5770  
* **California WIC App:** Search “California WIC” in the Apple App Store or Google Play.  
* **Online FAQs & Forms (multiple languages):** <https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/CFH/DWICSN/Pages/HowCanIGetWIC.aspx>  
* **General Benefits Help (CalWORKs, Medi‑Cal, etc.):** <https://www.calworks.org>  

---

### You’re Not Alone  

Losing a job can feel overwhelming, but California has a network of assistance programs. Getting started with WIC can give you healthy food for you and your little ones right away, while you explore other supports. If you have any questions about the paperwork or need help finding a nearby office, don’t hesitate to call the toll‑free number or ask a caseworker for a language interpreter—counties are required to provide assistance in your preferred language. Good luck, and take it one step at a time!

## Quick Ways to Get Rent Help in California  

| What you can do | How to start | Typical timeline |
|----------------|--------------|------------------|
| **Call 211** – the state’s 24‑hour referral line | Dial **211** or visit the [211 website](https://www.211.org/get-help/housing-expenses). A live worker will ask about your income, household size, and rent amount, then connect you with local emergency‑rental programs, charities, or government funds. | **Same‑day** referral; program processing can take **1‑4 weeks** depending on the agency. |
| **Apply for Emergency Rental Assistance (ERA)** – state‑ and county‑run funds created after COVID‑19 | 1. Locate your county’s ERA portal (search “[County] California Emergency Rental Assistance” or ask 211). 2. Create an online account or request a paper application. 3. Submit required documents (see list below). | Most counties aim to **process within 30‑45 days**, but busy periods may be longer. |
| **CalWORKs (California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids)** – cash aid that can be used for rent | Call your local County Social Services Agency or apply online at the [CalWORKs portal](https://www.cdss.ca.gov/calworks). | Initial eligibility decision usually **within 30 days**; ongoing monthly benefits start after that. |
| **HUD‑approved housing counseling** – free help to understand options and paperwork | Find a counselor via the HUD website’s [search tool](https://www.hud.gov/offices/hsg/sfh/hcc/hcs). Call the HOPE™ Hotline (888‑995‑HOPE) for immediate assistance. | Counseling is **immediate**; they can help you complete ERA or CalWORKs applications. |
| **Utility & Energy assistance** (if you also need help with bills) | Apply for **LIHEAP** or the **Weatherization Assistance Program** through your local agency. Links at the bottom of this guide. | Usually **2‑4 weeks** for approval. |

---

## 1. Basic Eligibility (what most programs look for)

| Requirement | Typical rule (varies by county) |
|-------------|---------------------------------|
| **Residency** | Must live in the county where you apply. Proof of California residency (lease, utility bill, driver’s license, etc.) is required. |
| **Income** | Usually at to around **140 % of the federal poverty level (FPL)**, but many counties accept up to **200 %** for emergency help. Exact limits differ, so the county’s website will give the current figure. |
| **Housing status** | You must be at risk of eviction or already behind on rent (often ≤ 60 days). |
| **Citizenship** | U.S. citizens, permanent residents, or certain qualified non‑citizens (e.g., refugees, DACA) are eligible for most state funds. |
| **Other assistance** | If you already receive CalWORKs, SSI, or SNAP, you may get priority, but you can still apply for additional emergency rent help. |

---

## 2. Step‑by‑Step Process for Emergency Rental Assistance

1. **Gather proof of residency and rent**  
   * Current lease or rental agreement  
   * Recent rent receipt or a written statement from your landlord showing the amount owed  
   * Utility bill, driver’s license, or state ID with your address  

2. **Collect income documentation**  
   * Most recent pay stubs (or proof of unemployment benefits)  
   * Tax return or W‑2 if you were recently employed  
   * Any other benefit statements (CalWORKs, SSI, SNAP)  

3. **Call 211 (or visit 211.org)**  
   * Tell the specialist you need **emergency rental assistance**.  
   * They will give you the direct link or phone number for your county’s ERA program and may schedule a virtual or in‑person intake.  

4. **Complete the county application**  
   * Fill out the online form (or paper form if required).  
   * Upload or attach the documents from steps 1‑2.  
   * Some counties ask for a **letter from your landlord** confirming the risk of eviction.  

5. **Submit and track**  
   * After you submit, you’ll receive a confirmation number.  
   * Most portals let you check status online; otherwise, the 211 worker can follow up for you.  

6. **Receive the funds**  
   * Funds are usually sent **directly to the landlord** on your behalf.  
   * You’ll get a notice of the amount paid and any remaining balance you must cover.  

---

## 3. Documents Most Counties Require

| Category | Examples |
|----------|----------|
| **Proof of residence** | Lease, rental agreement, recent utility bill, mail with your name and address |
| **Proof of rent owed** | Rent ledger, landlord’s written statement, eviction notice, rent receipt |
| **Income proof** | Pay stubs, unemployment benefits award letter, Social Security/SSI award letter, CalWORKs benefit notice |
| **Identification** | Driver’s license, state ID, or passport with current address |
| **Household composition** | Birth certificates or school enrollment letters for children living with you (if asked) |
| **Other assistance** | Copies of any other public benefits you receive (optional but may speed review) |

---

## 4. Timeline Overview (what to expect)

| Action | Approximate time |
|--------|------------------|
| **Initial 211 referral** | Immediate (same call) |
| **Application submission** | As soon as you gather docs (often 1‑3 days) |
| **County review** | 2‑4 weeks on average; some counties have “fast‑track” for evictions within 7‑10 days |
| **Payment to landlord** | Within a few days of approval |
| **Follow‑up** | 211 or county case manager may contact you to confirm payment or request additional info |

*If you face an imminent eviction (e.g., a court date within a week), tell the 211 worker right away—they can flag your case for “expedited” processing.*

---

## 5. County‑Specific Note  

California’s emergency‑rental assistance is **run by each county**, so the exact income limits, required forms, and processing speed can differ. Use the 211 referral or search “**[Your County] California Emergency Rental Assistance**” to find the most current local portal.  

If you move to a new county during the process, you’ll need to re‑apply with the new county’s program.

---

## 6. Other Programs That May Help You

| Program | Who it helps | How to apply |
|---------|--------------|--------------|
| **CalWORKs** | Low‑income families with children (also adults without children in some cases) | Call your County Social Services Agency or apply online at the [CalWORKs site](https://www.cdss.ca.gov/calworks). |
| **LIHEAP (Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program)** | Helps pay heating, cooling, and emergency energy bills | Find your local LIHEAP office via the [USDA portal](https://www.acf.hhs.gov/ocs/initiatives/liheap). |
| **Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP)** | Free home upgrades that lower energy costs | Contact your state’s WAP office (search “California Weatherization Assistance”). |
| **HUD‑approved Housing Counseling** | Free budgeting help, foreclosure prevention, and guidance on rental assistance | Locate a counselor at the [HUD website](https://www.hud.gov/offices/hsg/sfh/hcc/hcs). |
| **Veterans’ Emergency Housing** (if you’re a veteran) | Specialized housing and cash assistance | Call the VA Homeless Veterans Hotline 1‑877‑424‑3838. |
| **Nonprofit & faith‑based charities** (e.g., Salvation Army, Catholic Charities) | Direct cash grants or short‑term rentals | Ask 211 for local agency referrals. |

---

## 7. Helpful Tips

* **Talk to your landlord ASAP** – many landlords will accept a payment plan if they know you’re seeking assistance.

question: What are the income limits for Unemployment Insurance?
answer:
## How Unemployment Insurance (UI) Works in California  

**Unemployment Insurance** gives you a temporary cash benefit while you look for new work.  
You do **not** need to stay under a fixed “income limit” to qualify, but you **must have earned enough wages** during a prior period (the **base period**) to be eligible.

---

### 1. Eligibility – What the state looks at  

| Requirement | What it means for you |
|-------------|-----------------------|
| **Earned enough wages** | You need a minimum amount of earnings in the **base period** (the first 4 of the last 5 completed calendar quarters before you filed). The exact amount changes each year, but roughly it’s comparable to earning about **$1,200‑$1,500 in total wages** during that period. |
| **Worked in California** | Your wages must have been earned from a job covered by California payroll taxes. |
| **Lost work through no fault of your own** | Being laid off, having hours reduced, or being let go for reasons not related to misconduct. |
| **Able, available, and actively looking for work** | You must be physically able to work, ready to accept a job, and certify that you’re looking for work each week. |
| **Legal work authorization** | You need a Social Security number and permission to work in the U.S. (citizens, permanent residents, or eligible non‑citizens). |

> **Note:** While the basic wage test is the same statewide, some counties may have additional outreach or rapid‑response programs for certain industries. Call your local **EDD office** if you hear about a county‑specific job‑training or “quick‑start” UI pilot.

---

### 2. How the wage test is calculated  

1. **Base period** – Usually the first 4 quarters of the last 5 quarters before you apply.  
2. **Quarterly earnings** – The EDD looks at the highest‑earning quarter in that period.  
3. **Minimum earnings** – You must have earned **at least $1,300** (or the equivalent in your county’s wage‑base) in **one** of those quarters and at least **$1,800** total in the whole base period.  
   *These amounts are adjusted each year; the EDD website has the current numbers.*  

If you don’t meet the standard test, you might still qualify through an **alternative base period** (the most recent 4 quarters) or if you’re a **seasonal worker**.  

---

### 3. Steps to Apply  

1. **Gather required information**  
   - Social Security number  
   - Driver’s license or ID card number  
   - Last employer’s name, address, phone, and dates of employment  
   - Your last pay stub or W‑2 (to verify wages)  
   - Bank account and routing number (for direct deposit)  

2. **Create a myEDD account** – Go to the [EDD UI Online portal](https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/) and register.  

3. **File the claim** – Choose “Apply for Unemployment Insurance” and follow the prompts. You can also apply by phone (1‑800‑300‑5616) or by fax/mail using form **DE 1101I**.  

4. **Register with CalJOBS** – Within 7 days of filing, you must create a free CalJOBS profile and upload a résumé.  

5. **Certify each week** – Log in to UI Online every 2 weeks (or as instructed) to answer a short questionnaire confirming you’re job‑searching and reporting any earnings.  

---

### 4. Documents You May Need  

| Document | Why it matters |
|----------|----------------|
| **Pay stubs / W‑2** | Prove the wages you earned in the base period. |
| **Separation notice** (if you have one) | Shows the date you left work. |
| **Bank account info** | For direct‑deposit of benefits. |
| **Proof of identity** (driver’s license, state ID) | Confirms you are the claimant. |
| **Proof of citizenship or work authorization** | Required for eligibility. |

You can usually upload these documents directly in your UI Online account.

---

### 5. How Long It Takes  

| Process | Typical Timeline |
|---------|-------------------|
| **Initial claim processing** | About **3 weeks** from the date you submit the application (may be longer during high volume periods). |
| **First benefit payment** | After your claim is approved, the first payment is usually **within 7‑10 days** of your first successful weekly certification. |
| **Weekly certification** | Must be done **every 2 weeks** (or as the UI portal indicates) to keep receiving benefits. |

---

### 6. Other Benefits You May Want to Consider  

| Program | Who might qualify | How it helps |
|---------|-------------------|--------------|
| **CalFresh (SNAP)** | Low‑income households, including those receiving UI. | Monthly food assistance; eligibility limits use your UI income as part of the calculation. |
| **California Training Benefits** | UI claimants who enroll in approved training or community‑college courses. | Allows you to keep receiving UI while you learn new skills. |
| **Paid Family Leave (PFL) & Disability Insurance (DI)** | If you need time off to care for a family member or have a medical condition. | Provides partial wage replacement; may be combined with UI in certain cases. |
| **Emergency Rental Assistance** | Households facing eviction after losing income. | Cash assistance for rent and utilities; county programs vary. |
| **Self‑Employment Assistance (SEA)** | Former UI recipients who want to start a small business. | Provides a stipend while you develop your business plan. |

> **Tip:** Applying for one program does **not** stop you from applying for another. Many agencies let you apply simultaneously, and they’ll let you know if there’s any conflict.

---

### 7. Getting Help  

- **Phone:** Call the UI Customer Service line at **1‑800‑300‑5616** (English/Spanish). Multilingual options are listed on the EDD site.  
- **Online:** Use the **“Contact Us”** feature in your UI Online account.  
- **In‑person:** Visit your local **EDD office** (search “EDD office near me” for address and hours).  
- **Community partners:** Non‑profits such as **211.org**, local **career centers**, and **legal aid societies** can help you complete the application.  

---

### 8. Quick Recap  

- There is **no set income ceiling** for UI; you need to have **earned enough wages** in the base period (about $1,300 in one quarter and $1,800 total).  
- Apply online or by phone, then certify every two weeks.  
- Keep your documents handy and register with CalJOBS.  
- While you receive UI, you may also be eligible for CalFresh, training benefits, and other assistance.  

If you have any specific questions about your wage history or need help with the application, feel free to reach out to the EDD or a local community service agency. We're here to help you get back on your feet.  

---  

**Helpful Links**  

- [Apply for UI – myEDD portal](https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/)  
- [CalFresh eligibility & application](https://www.getcalfresh.org/)  
- [California Training Benefits](https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/training/)  
- [Find your nearest EDD office](https://edd.ca.gov/office-locator/)

## How to Apply for **CalWORKs** Benefits  

You can start the application **online** **or** **in person**.  

| Method | What to Do | Who to Contact |
|--------|------------|----------------|
| **Online** | Go to **[BenefitsCal.com](https://www.benefitscal.com)** and click **“Apply for CalWORKs.”** Fill out the short questionnaire (about 30‑60 minutes). | If you have questions while you’re online, call your **County Social Services Agency** (the phone number is listed on the BenefitsCal site). |
| **In‑person** | Visit your local **County Welfare / Social Services Office**. Bring a copy of the application form (you can print it at the office or download it from the county’s website). | Find the nearest office on the **[CDSS County Offices page](https://www.cdss.ca.gov/County-Offices)** or call the county’s main number. |

### General Steps  

1. **Gather Needed Documents** (see list below).  
2. **Complete the application** (online or paper).  
3. **Attend an eligibility interview** (usually a phone call or a brief meeting at the office).  
4. **Receive a notice** about your eligibility and benefit amount.  
5. **Start receiving cash aid** on an EBT card or direct deposit, plus any other approved services (housing help, child‑care, job training, etc.).

### Typical Documents You’ll Need  

- Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID, or passport)  
- Social Security numbers for all household members  
- Proof of California residence (lease, utility bill, or mail)  
- Recent pay stubs, unemployment benefits statement, or other income proof  
- Recent bank statements (to show assets)  
- Birth certificates for children (to verify age)  
- If you’re a student, a school enrollment verification  

*Your county caseworker will tell you if any additional paperwork is required.*  

### How Long It Usually Takes  

- **Application submission:** 30‑60 minutes (online) or one visit to the office.  
- **Interview scheduling:** County staff typically call within **1‑2 weeks**.  
- **Decision notice:** Usually sent within **2‑4 weeks** after the interview, but timing can vary by county.  

### County‑Specific Notes  

- Every California county has its own **Welfare Office**, so contact information (phone numbers, office hours, and exact location) can differ.  
- Some counties offer **language assistance** or **translation services** if you need help completing the form in another language.  
- Certain counties may have **additional local programs** that work together with CalWORKs (e.g., extra housing vouchers or child‑care subsidies). Ask your caseworker about any county‑specific options.  

### Other Programs You Might Want to Explore  

Even if you’re waiting for CalWORKs, the following state programs can provide immediate help:  

| Program | Who It Helps | How to Apply |
|---------|--------------|--------------|
| **Medi‑Cal** (California’s Medicaid) | Low‑income individuals and families for health coverage | Apply online at **[Medi‑Cal Access Center](https://www.medicalaccess.ca.gov)** or at your county office |
| **CalFresh** (SNAP) | Food assistance for households meeting income limits | Apply through **BenefitsCal.com** (same portal as CalWORKs) |
| **Cal **Lifeline** | Discounted phone or internet service | Apply online if you’re enrolled in a qualifying program like CalWORKs, Medi‑Cal, or CalFresh |
| **California Alternate Rates for Energy (CARE)** | Discount on electricity and gas bills | Apply through your utility company or online at **[CARE](https://www.care.org)** |
| **Emergency Housing Assistance** | Short‑term shelter, security deposits, or rent help | Ask your county welfare office; many counties run a **Homeless Assistance** program through CalWORKs |

### Quick Contact Checklist  

- **Online portal:** [BenefitsCal.com – Apply for CalWORKs](https://www.benefitscal.com)  
- **County office finder:** [CDSS County Offices](https://www.cdss.ca.gov/County-Offices)  
- **Phone (statewide help line):** 1‑800‑442‑4022 (press “1” for CalWORKs)  

---

**You’re not alone.** Asking for help is a strong first step, and the county staff are there to guide you through the process. If anything feels confusing, call your local office—they can walk you through each step and answer any questions you have. Good luck, and take one step at a time!

question: What documents do I need for Unemployment Insurance and how do I apply?
answer:
## How to Apply for Unemployment Insurance (UI) in California  

### 1. Gather the basics you’ll need  

| Item | Why it’s needed |
|------|-----------------|
| **Social Security number** | Identifies you to the state. |
| **EDD Customer Account Number (EDDCAN)** – you’ll get this by mail after you file your first claim (usually within 10 business days). | Used to log in to **UI Online** (myEDD). |
| **Proof you’re allowed to work in the U.S.** (U.S. passport, green card, work visa, etc.) | Shows you have legal work authorization. |
| **Recent pay‑stubs, W‑2s, or a “final pay statement” from your last employer** | Shows you earned enough wages in the base period (the first 4‑quarter of the last 18 months). |
| **Bank account routing & account number** (or mailing address if you want a paper check) | Where your weekly benefit payment will be sent. |
| **Contact information** – phone, email, current address | EDD will use this to send you notices and to verify your identity if needed. |
| **Any letters from your former employer** (e.g., termination notice, lay‑off notice) – optional but helpful | Explains why you are no longer working. |

> **Tip:** Even if you’re not sure you meet every requirement (e.g., you quit or were fired), **apply anyway**. The EDD will tell you if you qualify.

### 2. Step‑by‑step application process  

| Step | What to do | How long it takes |
|------|------------|-------------------|
| **1. Create a myEDD account** | Go to **[myEDD.gov](https://myedd.ca.gov)** and follow the prompts. You’ll need an email address and a password. | A few minutes. |
| **2. Start a new UI claim** | After logging in, click **“File a New Claim”** and answer the short questionnaire. | 10‑15 minutes. |
| **3. Submit required info** | Enter your SSN, EDDCAN (if you already have one), employer details, and banking info. Upload scans or photos of your pay‑stubs/W‑2s if asked. | 5‑10 minutes. |
| **4. Get your EDDCAN (if you don’t have one yet)** | The EDD will mail you a **Customer Account Number Notification (DE 5614)** within about 10 business days. Keep this letter safe – you’ll need it to log into UI Online. | 1‑2 weeks (mail). |
| **5. Register for UI Online (optional but recommended)** | Use your EDDCAN to log into **UI Online** (myEDD → UI Online). This lets you view claim status, certify for benefits, and report any work or income. | Immediate after you receive the number. |
| **6. Certify for benefits every two weeks** | Log into UI Online (or call **1‑866‑333‑4606** for Tele‑Cert) to answer a few questions and confirm you’re still unemployed and looking for work. | 5‑10 minutes each certification. |
| **7. Keep a work‑search record** (if asked) | Some counties require you to list the jobs you applied for each week. UI Online has a built‑in screen for this; you can also keep a simple notebook. | Ongoing. |

#### Alternative ways to apply  

* **By phone:** Call the UI claims line **1‑800‑300‑5616** (English/Spanish) or the language‑specific numbers listed in the source.  
* **By fax or mail:** Download and print the **Unemployment Insurance Application (DE 1101I)**, fill it out, and fax or mail it to the address on the form. This method is slower than online.  

### 3. Basic eligibility you should meet  

* You are **totally or partially unemployed** through **no fault of your own** (lay‑off, reduction in hours, quit for good cause, etc.).  
* You are **physically able** to work and **available** for work.  
* You are **actively looking for work** each week (unless you’re on a special program).  
* You have earned **enough wages** during the “base period” (the first four quarters of the last 18 months).  
* You have a **valid Social Security number** and **legal work authorization**.  

If any of these sound uncertain, still **file a claim**; the EDD will review your situation.

### 4. Timelines to keep in mind  

| Action | Approximate time frame |
|--------|------------------------|
| **File the claim** | Immediately after losing a job (online is fastest). |
| **Receive EDDCAN** | ~10 business days after the claim is filed. |
| **First benefit payment** | Usually within **2‑3 weeks** after your claim is approved and you have certified for the first week. |
| **Request additional documents** (e.g., identity verification) | Respond within **3 days** to the online request or **7 days** to any mailed form to avoid delays. |
| **Certification every two weeks** | Do it **by the deadline shown in your UI Online account** (typically the Friday of the week you’re claiming). Missing a deadline can pause your payment. |

### 5. County‑specific notes  

* **Some counties have extra “work‑search” documentation requirements** (e.g., a written log or a web‑based portal).  
* **Benefit award amounts** may vary slightly because of local wage data, but the **state formula** is the same everywhere.  
* If you need help in person, contact your local **America’s Job Center of California**—they can assist with paperwork and explain any county rules.

### 6. Other programs that might help while you’re unemployed  

| Program | What it provides | Who should consider it |
|---------|------------------|------------------------|
| **CalFresh (SNAP)** | Monthly food assistance. | Low‑income households, regardless of job status. |
| **Medi‑Cal** | Free or low‑cost health coverage. | Residents with limited income or assets. |
| **California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids (CalWORKs)** | Cash aid and services for families with children. | Parents/guardians who meet income limits. |
| **Portable Benefits for gig and independent‑contract workers** | Unemployment, disability, and health benefits for qualifying contractors. | People who were classified as independent contractors. |
| **Local Rental Assistance Programs** | Help paying rent or utility bills. | Tenants facing eviction due to loss of income. |
| **Training & Re‑employment Programs (e.g., Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act – WIOA)** | Job training, apprenticeships, and career counseling. | Anyone looking to gain new skills or certifications. |

You can apply for many of these programs **online at the same time** as your UI claim. They often share the same documentation (ID, income proof, residency proof), so having those ready helps.

### 7. Quick checklist before you start  

- [ ] Social Security number  
- [ ] Recent pay‑stubs / W‑2s (last 12 months)  
- [ ] Bank account info (or address for paper checks)  
- [ ] Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID, passport)  
- [ ] Employer name, address, dates of employment, and reason for separation (if you have a termination or lay‑off letter)  
- [ ] Email address (to create a myEDD account)  

### 8. Where to get help  

* **Online:** Use the **Ask EDD** portal on myEDD for live chat or email support.  
* **Phone:** Call **1‑800‑300‑5616** (Monday‑Friday, 8 am‑5 pm PT). Interpreter services are free for many languages.  
* **In‑person:** Visit your nearest **America’s Job Center of California** (free computers, staff assistance, and paper‑application help).  
* **For the hearing‑impaired:** Call **1‑800‑815‑9387** (TTY) or use **California Relay Service (711)**.  

---

**You’re not alone.** Applying for unemployment can feel overwhelming, but the steps above break it into manageable pieces. Start by creating a myEDD account and filing your claim online—most people receive their first payment within a few weeks. If you run into a snag, reach out to the EDD or your local job center for help. Good luck, and take one step at a time.

question: Laid off this month. I need help paying for food. Can I get help quickly? What can I qualify for and how do I apply in my county?
answer:
## You can get food help right away  

When you lose a job you can still qualify for **CalFresh** (California’s food assistance program).  If you need food now, ask for **Expedited Service** – many counties can give you a benefit card within **3 days**.

### Basic eligibility  
| What the county looks at | Typical rule (may vary by county) |
|--------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| **Income** – money you earn, unemployment benefits, SSI, etc. | If your wages stopped this month, the county only counts any final pay you received in the **last 30 days**.  Ongoing benefits are based on the income you currently have. |
| **Household size** – who lives with you and shares food | Larger households get a higher benefit amount. |
| **Resources** – savings, bank accounts, etc. | Most families have a small resource limit (usually $2,500‑$3,500).  Many counties exclude your home and car. |
| **Citizenship/Immigration status** | You must be a U.S. citizen, national, or have an eligible immigration status.  Counties must provide help in your native language if you ask. |

*If you are a student, you may still qualify if you meet one of the student exceptions (e.g., work ≥ 20 hrs/week, receive work‑study, or are on a cash‑assistance program).*

### Documents you’ll need
- **Proof of identity** (driver’s license, state ID, or passport)  
- **Proof of residence** (utility bill, lease, or mail with your address)  
- **Proof of income** for the last 30 days (final pay stub, unemployment award letter, or a written statement from your former employer with the last work date)  
- **Social Security numbers** for everyone in the household

### How to apply in your county
1. **Create an online account** at **[BenefitsCal.com](https://www.benefitscal.com)** – you can start the application, upload documents, and check status.  
2. **Select “Apply for CalFresh.”**  The system will ask for the items above and will let you request **Expedited Service**.  
3. **Call or visit your local County Human Services Agency (HSA)** if you need help, an interpreter, or have trouble online.  Look up the phone number on the county’s website or on the BenefitsCal portal.  
4. **Submit the application** and any required documents.  The county has up to **30 days** to decide, but with Expedited Service you should hear back in **3 days**.  
5. **If approved**, you’ll receive an EBT card in the mail (or a temporary card if you’re approved the same day).  Load it with your first benefit amount and start buying groceries.

|---------|----------------|---------------|

| **Medi‑Cal** | Free or low‑cost health coverage | Most Californians with low income; includes doctor visits, prescriptions, and emergency care |
| **Unemployment Insurance (UI)** | Weekly cash benefits while you look for work | You must have earned enough wages in the past 12 months and be laid off through no fault of your own |
| **LIHEAP / WAP** | Help with heating, cooling, and electricity bills | Low‑income households; apply through your local utility or county social services |

### Quick‑step checklist

2. **Create a BenefitsCal account** and start the CalFresh application.  
3. **Ask for Expedited Service** (food card within 3 days).  
4. **Call your County HSA** if you need help with language, paperwork, or want to explore CalWORKs, Medi‑Cal, or emergency cash aid.  
5. **Keep a copy of everything** you submit – the county may ask for more proof later.

answer:
## What Is the California Earned Income Tax Credit (CalEITC)?

The **CalEITC** is a cash‑back credit that you can claim on your California state tax return.  
It reduces any tax you owe and can give you a refund if the credit is larger than your tax bill.  

- It is **not** a program that pays you right away – you get the money when you file your state tax return.  
- The amount you may receive depends on **your earned income** and **how many qualifying children you have**.

## Who Can Claim CalEITC?

| Requirement | What it means for you |
|-------------|-----------------------|
| **Age** | You must be **18 years or older**, or have a qualifying child. |
| **Income** | Earned income (wages, self‑employment, etc.) must be **at least $1** and **no more than $31,950** for the tax year. |
| **Residency** | You lived in California for **more than half the year**. |
| **Social Security** | You, your spouse/registered domestic partner (RDP), and any qualifying children must have a valid **Social Security Number (SSN)** or **ITIN**. |
| **Dependent status** | You cannot be claimed as a qualifying child on someone else’s return, and you can’t be claimed as a dependent **unless** you have a qualifying child. |
| **Filing status** | Single, married filing jointly, married filing separately (with extra rules), or head of household. |

> **Note:** The exact credit amount changes each year. Use the CalEITC calculator on the FTB site to see an estimate for your situation.

## How to Apply for CalEITC

1. **Check your eligibility** – use the simple checklist above or the online calculator.  
2. **Gather needed documents**  
   - Recent **pay stubs** or **W‑2s** showing earned income.  
   - Your **Social Security Number** (or ITIN).  
   - **Tax return** from the year you are filing (2024 tax year, filed by April 15 2025).  
   - If you have a spouse/RDP, their SSN and income information too.  
3. **Choose a filing method**  
   - **Free tax help**: Find a nearby **VITA/TCE** site (Volunteer Income Tax Assistance / Tax Counseling for the Elderly) — they will prepare your return for free if you make $67 K or less.  
     - Locate a site: [FTB Free Tax Help Locator](https://www.ftb.ca.gov/help/free-tax-help/index.html?WT.mc_id=CAGov_Service_VITA)  
   - **Online software**: Many free‑file programs include the CalEITC automatically.  
   - **Tax professional**: If you prefer, you can hire a CPA or tax preparer.  
4. **File your California state tax return** (Form 540 or 540‑NR).  
   - On the return, fill out the **CalEITC worksheet**. The software or VITA volunteer will handle this for you.  
5. **Receive your credit**  
   - If you have a refund, the state will mail a check or deposit it directly into your bank account.  
   - If you owe tax, the credit will reduce what you owe.

### Timeline

| When | What happens |
|------|--------------|
| **January – April** | Gather documents and file your 2024 California tax return (deadline ≈ April 15, 2025). |
| **After filing** | The Franchise Tax Board processes your return (usually 2‑4 weeks). |
| **Refund** | If you’re getting a refund, the money arrives by direct deposit or mail after processing. |

## Other Programs You Might Need Right Now

Losing a job can affect many parts of your budget. While you’re waiting for your tax refund, consider these California assistance programs:

| Program | Who can apply | What it helps with | How to apply |
|---------|---------------|-------------------|--------------|
| **Unemployment Insurance (UI)** | You were laid off, earned enough wages, and are able and available to work. | Weekly benefit payments while you look for work. | Apply online at **myEDD** – fastest way. Start here: [Apply for UI](https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/step-2-apply/) |
| **CalFresh ( SNAP )** | Low‑income households; recent loss of income counts as 0 $ income for the first month. | Monthly food assistance cards. | Find your county’s CalFresh office: [GetCalFresh.org](https://www.getcalfresh.org/en/faq) |
| **California Training Benefits (CTB)** | You have an active UI claim and want to enroll in approved training. | Up to $6,000 for tuition, books, fees. | Contact EDD before the 16th week of UI benefits. Details: [CTB info](https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/Eligible_Training_Types_for_CTB/) |
| **Low‑Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP)** | Low‑income households needing help with heating/cooling bills. | Grants to pay utility bills. | Locate your state office: [LIHEAP help](https://www.usa.gov/help-with-energy-bills) |
| **Free Tax Help (VITA/TCE)** | Income ≤ $67 K, disability, limited English, or senior (60 +). | Free preparation of federal and California returns, including CalEITC. | Find a site: [VITA/TCE Locator](https://www.ftb.ca.gov/help/free-tax-help/index.html?WT.mc_id=CAGov_Service_VITA) |

## Quick Checklist for CalEITC

- [ ] Age ≥ 18 **or** have a qualifying child  
- [ ] Earned income ≤ $31,950 (check your W‑2)  
- [ ] Lived in CA > ½ year  
- [ ] Valid SSN/ITIN for you and any dependents  
- [ ] Not claimed as someone else’s dependent (unless you have a qualifying child)  
- [ ] File your 2024 CA tax return by **April 15 2025** (or request an extension)  

## Need Help Getting Started?

- **Call the EDD** (UI questions) at **1‑800‑300‑5616** (8 am‑5 pm PT, Mon‑Fri).  
- **Visit a local America’s Job Center** for in‑person assistance with UI, training, and job search.  
- **Use the free tax help locator** above to find a VITA/TCE site near you.

---

**You’re not alone.** Many Californians face layoffs each year, and these programs exist to help you get back on your feet. Start with the UI claim right away, then gather your tax documents and claim the CalEITC when you file. If you have any more questions, feel free to ask!

question: I have a toddler and just lost my job. What can I qualify for and how do I apply?
answer:
## You’ve lost your job and have a toddler – What help is available in California? First, take a deep breath. California has many programs that can give you **money for food, health care, child care, and training** while you look for a new job. Below is a quick guide to the main options, who can qualify, what you need to apply, and the basic steps to get started. | Program | What it provides | Who may be eligible* | Main documents you’ll need | |---------|-------------------|----------------------|----------------------------| | **Unemployment Insurance (UI)** | Weekly cash payments while you’re looking for work. | You were employed and earned enough wages in the last 12‑18 months; you are able and available to work. | • Last 4‑6 pay stubs or earnings record
• Employer’s name & contact info
• Social Security Number (SSN) | | **CalWORKs (California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids)** | Cash aid, health coverage, food assistance, and **child‑care vouchers** for families with children under 18 (or up to 21 with a disability). | Low‑income households with a child; you must be a California resident and meet citizenship/immigration rules. | • Proof of identity (driver’s license, ID card, or passport)
• Proof of income (pay stubs, unemployment award, SSI, etc.)
• Proof of residence (utility bill, lease)
• Birth certificate or adoption papers for your toddler | | **CalFresh (SNAP/food stamps)** | Monthly benefit card to buy groceries. | Low‑to‑moderate income households; no asset limit for most families. | • Same documents as CalWORKs (income & residency proof) | | **Medi‑Cal** | Free or low‑cost health coverage (doctor visits, prescriptions, hospital care). | Low‑income adults, children, pregnant people, and families. | • Proof of identity & residency
• Income information (including any UI benefits) | | **WIC (Women, Infants & Children)** | Supplemental nutrition (milk, formula, fruits/veggies) and breastfeeding support for pregnant people, new parents, and children ≤ 5 y. | Low‑to‑moderate income; you must be enrolled in Medi‑Cal, CalWORKs, or CalFresh (or meet income test). | • Proof of identity & residency
• Recent pregnancy or birth certificate
• Income proof | | **Child‑Care Assistance (through CalWORKs or local R&R agencies)** | Pays for licensed child‑care while you work, go to school, or attend job‑training. | Parents who are working or in a county‑approved welfare‑to‑work program. | • Enrollment in CalWORKs or welfare‑to‑work
• Child‑care provider’s information (license number) | | **Job‑Training Programs** (e.g., **EDD “Trade‑Adjustment Assistance”, “CalWORKs Welfare‑to‑Work”, “TANF job‑training”) | Free or low‑cost classes, apprenticeships, and on‑the‑job training that can lead to a new career. | Usually tied to UI, CalWORKs, or TANF enrollment and a demonstrated need for new skills. | • Proof of UI, CalWORKs, or TANF participation
• High‑school diploma or GED (often)
• Personal identification | \*Eligibility can vary a little by **county** (especially for CalWORKs cash aid amounts and child‑care vouchers). Your county social‑services office will give the exact numbers for where you live. --- ## How to Apply – Step‑by‑Step ### 1. Gather Your Documents - **ID** (driver’s license, state ID, or passport) - **Social Security Number** (or “no‑SSN” proof if you don’t have one) - **Proof of income** (most recent pay stubs, unemployment award letter, or a statement showing no income) - **Proof of residence** (utility bill, lease, or mail addressed to you) - **Child’s birth certificate** (or other proof of relationship) ### 2. Apply for Unemployment Insurance (UI) 1. Go to the **EDD website**: 2. Click **“Apply Now”** and create an account on **BenefitsCal.com**. 3. Follow the online prompts (you’ll need the documents above). 4. After you submit, you’ll receive a **Confirmation Number**. 5. **Certify** each two‑week period (you can do this online or by phone). **Timeline:** You should get a **first payment within 2–3 weeks** after your claim is approved, as long as you certify on time. ### 3. Apply for CalWORKs (Cash & Child‑Care) 1. Find your **County Social Services Office** (search “CalWORKs + [Your County]”). 2. Call or go in person to request an **application** (many counties also have an online portal). 3. Fill out the form and schedule an **eligibility interview** (usually within 1–2 weeks). 4. Bring the documents listed above to the interview. **Timeline:** After the interview, you’ll hear back **within a few weeks**. If approved, cash aid can start **the first month after your interview**; child‑care vouchers are issued shortly after. ### 4. Apply for CalFresh (Food Assistance) 1. Go to **GetCalFresh.org**: 2. Click **“Apply”** and follow the steps to create an account on **BenefitsCal.com**. 3. Submit the same income and residency documents. **Timeline:** Most counties make a decision **within 30 days** of receiving a complete application. You’ll get a **EBT card** if approved. ### 5. Apply for Medi‑Cal (Health Coverage) 1. Visit **Medi‑Cal’s online portal**: or call **1‑800‑541‑5555**. 2. Fill out the application (you can do it online, by phone, or in person). **Timeline:** Coverage can start **the first day of the month** after approval (often within 2 weeks). ### 6. Apply for WIC (Nutrition for Mom & Child) 1. Locate your nearest **WIC office**: 2. Bring ID, proof of residence, pregnancy or birth documentation, and any current benefit statements (Medi‑Cal, CalWORKs, CalFresh). **Timeline:** After the eligibility interview (usually same‑day or within a week), you’ll receive a **WIC card** that can be used right away. ### 7. Look for Job‑Training Opportunities - **EDD’s CalJOBS**: – Register for free and see training listings. - **County Welfare‑to‑Work (WTW) office** – Ask about **CalWORKs WTW training vouchers** or **TANF training**. - **Trade‑Adjustment Assistance (TAA)** – If your layoff was due to foreign trade, ask your former employer or union to file a petition. **How to start:** Once you’re enrolled in UI, CalWORKs, or TANF, you can request a **training plan** from a caseworker. Many programs cover tuition, supplies, and even a **stipend** while you study. --- ## Tips to Keep Things Moving | What to do | Why it helps | |------------|--------------| | **Apply to every program you might qualify for** (UI, CalWORKs, CalFresh, Medi‑Cal, WIC) | Benefits can be stacked – you can receive UI *and* CalFresh, for example. | | **Keep copies of all paperwork** | If a county office needs another copy, you’ll have it ready. | | **Notify each agency when your income changes** (e.g., you start a part‑time job) | Keeps you from over‑receiving benefits and avoids repayment issues. | | **Ask your caseworker about “Emergency Assistance”** | Some counties have fast‑track cash help for families facing an immediate crisis (e.g., utility shut‑off). | | **Use the BenefitsCal.com “My Cases” portal** to track status for UI, CalFresh, and CalWORKs in one place. | Saves time and shows you what’s pending. | --- ## Other Programs That Might Be Helpful - **Housing Assistance** – Local public‑housing agencies (PHAs) offer **Section 8 vouchers** or **Emergency Rental Assistance**. Contact your city’s Housing Authority. - **California Family Leave (PFL)** – If you become a caregiver for a sick family member, you may get partial wages for up to 8 weeks. More at . - **Veterans’ Benefits** – If you are a veteran, the **VA** and California’s **Veterans Services** can provide additional cash, housing, and job‑training help. - **Self‑Employment Assistance** – Some counties run **self‑employment programs** that give a stipend while you start a small business. Ask your County Social Services office. --- ## Quick Checklist ``` [ ] Gather ID, SSN, proof of income, proof of residence, child's birth certificate [ ] Apply for UI on BenefitsCal.com [ ] Contact County CalWORKs office – request interview [ ] Submit CalFresh application on GetCalFresh.org [ ] Enroll in Medi‑Cal (Covered California or county office) [ ] Visit local WIC office [ ] Register on CalJOBS for training options [ ] Ask caseworker about emergency cash or housing help ``` --- ### You’re not alone Losing a job is stressful, especially with a toddler. California’s safety‑net programs are designed to keep families fed, healthy, and moving toward stable employment. Start with the **UI claim** (you can do it in minutes online) and then reach out to your **county social‑services office** for CalWORKs, CalFresh, and child‑care help. Each agency will walk you through the next steps. If you run into any roadblocks, you can call the **EDD Customer Service** at **1‑800‑480‑3287** (UI) or your **County Social Services Helpline** (often a toll‑free number listed on the county’s website). Friendly staff are there to help you fill out forms and answer questions. Take it one step at a time—you’ve already made the hardest move by reaching out for help. Good luck, and we hope you and your toddler get the support you need soon. 🌱

question: I need help finding affordable child care. What are my options?
answer:
## You’re Not Alone – Affordable Child‑Care Options in California

Losing a job can make finding child‑care feel overwhelming. Below is a quick guide to the main programs and resources that can help you pay for child‑care while you look for work, get training, or start a new job.  

| Program | Who Can Apply | What It Covers | How to Start | Typical Timeline* |
|---------|---------------|----------------|--------------|-------------------|
| **CalWORKs Child‑Care Assistance** | Current or former CalWORKs cash‑aid recipients who are working, in a **Welfare‑to‑Work** activity, or in a county‑approved training program. Pregnant/parenting teens in **Cal‑Learn** also qualify. | Up to the county‑set maximum for a chosen provider (licensed center, family‑care home, or a qualified family member/friend). | 1️⃣ Call your **County Social Services Agency** or visit in‑person. 2️⃣ Request a child‑care voucher or “payment‑by‑authorisation” form. 3️⃣ Work with a **Child‑Care Resource & Referral (R&R)** agency to pick a provider. | Usually 2–4 weeks after you submit all paperwork, but can vary by county. |
| **Alternative Payment Programs (APP) / Community‑Based Agencies** | Families who **don’t receive CalWORKs cash aid** but need help paying for child‑care. | Similar to CalWORKs assistance; many counties run APPs that pay the provider directly. | 1️⃣ Find your local APP agency (list below). 2️⃣ Call or email to ask about “child‑care assistance.” 3️⃣ Submit an application and proof of income. | 2–6 weeks, depending on county capacity. |
| **Child‑Care Resource & Referral (R&R) Services** | Anyone looking for affordable child‑care, even if you’re not eligible for financial assistance. | Free help locating licensed providers, subsidies, sliding‑scale options, and “wait‑list” information. | 1️⃣ Call **1‑800‑KIDS‑793** (toll‑free, English & Spanish). 2️⃣ Or go to **MyChildCarePlan.org** and enter your ZIP code to connect with a local specialist. | Immediate phone/email help; provider placements may take several weeks. |
| **California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids (CalWORKs) – Education/Training** | If you’re enrolling in a job‑training or education program, you can combine that with child‑care assistance. | Child‑care dollars are added to the education/training budget, so you can keep your child while you study. | Ask your caseworker to add a **Child‑Care Component** to your Individualized Plan. | Same as CalWORKs child‑care timeline. |
| **Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) – Emergency Child‑Care** | Families in a crisis (e.g., sudden loss of income) may qualify for a **short‑term** voucher. | Typically covers 1–2 months while you apply for longer‑term help. | Request an “emergency” voucher from your county office. | Usually processed within **5‑10 business days**. |

\*Timelines are approximate. **Each county may have different processing times**, so ask your local office for the most current estimate.

---

## Steps to Get Help Right Now

1. **Gather Basic Documents**  
   - Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID, or passport)  
   - Proof of residence (utility bill, lease, or mail with your address)  
   - recent pay stubs or unemployment award notice (if you have them)  
   - Recent tax return or W‑2 (if you have them)  
   - Child’s birth certificate or school enrollment proof (to verify age)  

2. **Contact Your Local Child‑Care R&R Agency**  
   - Call **1‑800‑KIDS‑793** (available in English & Spanish).  
   - Or go to **[MyChildCarePlan.org](https://rrnetwork.org/family-services/find-child-care)**, enter your ZIP code, and request a live specialist.  

3. **Ask About Both CalWORKs and APP Options**  
   - Mention that you are **unemployed** and need child‑care while you look for work or training.  
   - The specialist will tell you which program(s) your county offers and start the application.  

4. **Complete the Application**  
   - Fill out the paper or online form the agency provides.  
   - Attach the documents from step 1.  
   - Sign any “authorization to release income information” forms.  

5. **Choose a Provider**  
   - You can pick any licensed child‑care center, family‑care home, or a qualified relative/friend (if approved).  
   - The R&R agency will give you a list of providers that accept the voucher or APP payment.  

6. **Wait for Approval**  
   - The county will review your paperwork and determine the dollar amount you qualify for.  
   - Once approved, they will send the payment directly to the provider (or give you a voucher to give them).  

7. **Keep Your Caseworker Updated**  
   - If your income or work status changes, let them know right away. This keeps your assistance active.  

---

## County‑Specific Contacts (APP/Child‑Care Agencies)

| County | Agency (Phone) | Notes |
|--------|----------------|-------|
| Los Angeles | **Child Care Resource Center** – 818‑756‑3360 | Large network of providers. |
| Fresno | **Central Valley Children’s Network** – 559‑456‑1100 | Handles both CalWORKs & APP. |
| San Diego | **San Diego County Office of Education – Child‑Care Services** – 619‑236‑5000 | Provides emergency vouchers. |
| Sacramento | **Sacramento County Human Services** – 916‑875‑3355 | Offers CalWORKs child‑care and emergency assistance. |
| Orange | **Orange County Human Services – Child‑Care** – 714‑834‑5000 | APP available for non‑CalWORKs families. |
| *All other counties* – Find your local agency by entering your ZIP code at **[MyChildCarePlan.org](https://rrnetwork.org/family-services/find-child-care)** or calling **1‑800‑KIDS‑793**. |

*The list above is a sample; every county has at least one R&R or APP office.*

---

## Other Resources You May Need While You’re Unemployed

| Need | Program | How to Apply |
|------|---------|--------------|
| **Unemployment Insurance (UI) benefits** | California Employment Development Department (EDD) | Apply online at **[edd.ca.gov](https://edd.ca.gov)**; you’ll need your most recent employment info and ID. |
| **Food assistance** | **CalFresh** (SNAP) | Call **1‑877‑847‑3663** or apply online at **[GetCalFresh.org](https://www.getcalfresh.org/en/faq)**. |
| **Cash aid while you job‑search** | **CalWORKs Cash Assistance** | Same county office that handles child‑care; ask about simultaneous cash and child‑care eligibility. |
| **Health coverage** | **Medi‑Cal** (California Medicaid) | Apply online at **[CoveredCA.com](https://www.coveredca.com)** or through your county social services office. |
| **Job training & education** | **CalWORKs Workforce Services** – includes tuition, books, transportation | Ask your caseworker to add a **Workforce Plan** to your CalWORKs case. |
| **Emergency shelter or housing help** | **County Homeless Services** | Call **2‑1‑1** for a local referral. |

---

## Quick Checklist

- [ ] Gather ID, residence proof, income/benefit documents, child’s birth certificate.  
- [ ] Call **1‑800‑KIDS‑793** or go to **MyChildCarePlan.org** to connect with a local specialist.  
- [ ] Ask about **CalWORKs child‑care**, **APP**, and any **emergency vouchers**.  
- [ ] Fill out the application and attach your documents.  
- [ ] Choose a licensed provider (or approved relative/friend).  
- [ ] Keep notes of who you spoke with, dates, and case numbers.  

---

### You’re Not Alone

California has many safety‑net programs designed to keep your child safe and cared for while you get back on your feet. Take the first step today by calling **1‑800‑KIDS‑793** or visiting **[MyChildCarePlan.org](https://rrnetwork.org/family-services/find-child-care)**. A caring specialist will guide you through the process and answer any questions you have.

*If you run into any roadblocks or need clarification, feel free to reach out again. We’re here to help you navigate the system.*
